This includes detailed insights into virus entry into host cells, synthesis of progeny viral components, assembly of new virions, and subsequent cell-to-cell transmission. This review summarizes the current literature on each of these aspects and discusses how this knowledge has been applied to develop novel vaccines against BTV and related orbiviruses. In addition, the review highlights important gaps in our understanding of virus replication within insect vectors, particularly Culicoides biting midges (gnats), at the molecular level. Addressing these gaps will provide valuable insights into orbivirus evolution, transmission, and the emergence of new viral strains.

title: Microregional RNA sequencing reveals layer-specific smooth muscle cell heterogeneity in human bicuspid aortic valve-associated aortic dilatation.
abstract: Smooth muscle cells in the human ascending aorta exhibit layer-specific heterogeneity; however, their molecular profiles and contribution to aortic diseases remain poorly understood. In this study, we applied microregional RNA sequencing to characterize layer-specific transcriptomic signatures and investigate the differences between bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) and tricuspid aortic valve (TAV) aortopathy. Dilated ascending aortic wall samples were obtained from nine patients who underwent ascending aorta replacement concomitant with aortic valve replacement: five with BAV and four with TAV. Microdissected tissues were collected from four distinct layers in media using a micro-punching device. RNA was extracted and sequenced, and the transcriptomic differences across the layers and between BAV- and TAV-dilated aortas were analyzed. Microregional RNA sequencing revealed significant upregulation of several extracellular matrix remodeling genes in the innermost layer, including FN1, VCAN, MGP, and POSTN. Among them, POSTN was further validated at the protein level, confirming its upregulation in the innermost layer, supporting the validity of this analysis. Next, the transcriptional differences between BAV- and TAV-dilated aortas across individual layers were analyzed. The gene expression differences were the most prominent in the innermost layer. Gene set enrichment analysis revealed that epithelial-mesenchymal transition and transforming growth factor β signaling-related genes were enriched in BAV-dilated aortas. In contrast, inflammation-related genes were enriched in TAV-dilated aortas. We also evaluated the pathways associated with the genes implicated in BAV formation to identify potential upstream mechanisms, revealing that mechanosensing-related genes are coordinately suppressed in BAV-dilated aortas. The present study demonstrated the application of microregional RNA sequencing to human aortic tissue, revealing layer-specific transcriptomic differences in aortic diseases. The differences in gene-set-level findings indicate distinct biological contexts and mechanisms in BAV- and TAV-dilated aortas, particularly in the innermost media layer. This approach is useful for assessing layer-specific profiles in aortic diseases. This study identified layer-specific heterogeneity within the human aorta, with molecular alterations in the innermost medial layer potentially contributing to differences between TAV- and BAV-associated aortopathy. The findings suggest that layer-specific transcriptome profiles differ across disease types. Accordingly, diagnostic approaches and therapeutic strategies may be more effective when tailored to specific aortic regions and their underlying molecular characteristics.

title: Molecular epidemiology and geographic distribution of Theileria spp. in Kazakhstan: a countrywide cattle survey and a southern sheep survey.
abstract: Theileriosis is endemic in Central Asia; however, the geographic distribution and genetic diversity of Theileria spp. in livestock in Kazakhstan remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to determine the occurrence, geographic distribution, and genetic diversity of Theileria spp. in cattle and sheep in Kazakhstan. Blood samples from 6,224 cattle from 172 settlements across all 17 provinces of Kazakhstan and 1,467 sheep from 52 settlements in five southern provinces were collected during July-August 2022 and 2023. Samples were screened using a genus-level PCR targeting the 28S ribosomal RNA (28S rRNA) gene, followed by bidirectional sequencing for species identification. Selected T. orientalis-positive samples were further characterized by major piroplasm surface protein (MPSP) genotyping. Among cattle, 2,142 out of 6,224 (34.4%) tested positive by PCR for at least one species of Theileria. Theileria annulata, T. orientalis, and T. sinensis were detected in 27.1, 15.1, and 0.5% of cattle, respectively. The simultaneous detection of two or three species of Theileria was recorded in 508 of 2,142 (23.7%) PCR-positive cattle. Theileria orientalis was detected in all 17 surveyed provinces, T. annulata in 16, and T. sinensis in five. MPSP analysis identified T. orientalis genotypes 1 ("Chitose"), 2 ("Ikeda"), and 3 ("Buffeli"). Among sheep, 169 out of 1,467 (11.5%) tested positive by PCR; T. ovis, Theileria sp. genotype OT3, and T. annulata were detected in 5.5, 4.4, and 2.6% of the animals examined, respectively. T. orientalis genotype 2 ("Ikeda"), T. sinensis, and Theileria sp. genotype OT3 were detected in Kazakhstan for the first time. The study demonstrated a widespread but geographically heterogeneous detection of Theileria species among sampled cattle across Kazakhstan and enabled the first molecular characterization of infections caused by Theileria species in sheep in that country. The detection of T. orientalis genotype 2 ("Ikeda"), T. sinensis, and Theileria sp. genotype OT3 expands the known diversity of Theileria species circulating in Central Asia. Since sampling was not conducted on a probabilistic basis, the observed PCR positivity should not be interpreted as representative of Theileria prevalence in the national livestock population. The data obtained serve as a starting point for targeted molecular surveillance of livestock and their associated tick vectors.

title: Lactobacillus mucosae extracellular vesicles improve metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease by activating the AMPK pathway via the gut-liver axis.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide but lacks effective therapies. Gut microbiota play a key role in MAFLD via the gut-liver axis, yet targeted interventions remain unclear. This study investigates the therapeutic effects and mechanisms of Lactobacillus mucosae (L. mucosae) and its extracellular vesicles (EVs) in MAFLD. At the clinical level, 16S rRNA sequencing was performed to analyze differences in gut microbiota composition between MAFLD patients and healthy controls, followed by the identification of a core probiotic strain, L. mucosae, using culture-based approaches. A high-fat diet-induced MAFLD mouse model was subsequently established to evaluate the therapeutic effects of L. mucosae, while free fatty acid-induced hepatocyte models were used to identify L. mucosae-EVs as the key active component. Mechanistic investigations and validation were further conducted in vivo and in vitro using RNA sequencing, qPCR, Western blot analyses, DIA-based EV proteomics, and Proteinase K-mediated EV protein functional assays. MAFLD patients showed reduced intestinal Lactobacillus abundance, negatively correlated with hepatic lipid parameters. L. mucosae administration alleviated steatosis, metabolic dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress in mice. In vitro, L. mucosae-EVs were confirmed as the main active component, and Proteinase K-pretreated EVs showed attenuated protective effects on hepatocytes. Mechanistically, L. mucosae-EVs activated hepatic AMPK signaling via the gut-liver axis, remodeled gut microbiota, and restored intestinal barrier integrity. This study systematically demonstrates for the first time that L. mucosae-EVs ameliorate MAFLD through multiple mechanisms, including gut microbiota remodeling, intestinal barrier restoration, and activation of hepatic AMPK signaling via the gut-liver axis. Proteinase K-mediated functional assays suggest that EV-associated protein cargo contributes, at least in part, to these protective effects. These findings provide a solid experimental foundation and theoretical basis for the development of precision microbiome-based therapeutic strategies for MAFLD based on L. mucosae and its EVs.

title: Iron Oxide Nanoparticles Alleviate Cold Stress in Rice by Reducing Oxidative Damage and Enhancing Antioxidant Defense Systems, and Transcriptional Networks.
abstract: Cold stress significantly impairs the rice (Oryza sativa L.) growth and yield, particularly in temperate regions where abrupt temperature fluctuations often occur during the early growth stages. Given the need for novel strategies to improve crop cold tolerance, we evaluated the efficacy of iron oxide nanoparticles (Fe2O3) in enhancing rice cold stress resilience. The reported mechanisms involve promoting plant growth and development, alleviating oxidative stress and inducing defense responses. Using RNA-seq, we analyzed the physiological and transcriptomic responses of rice to cold stress and Fe2O3 treatment. Under cold stress, the NPs elicited a strong antioxidant response-elevating superoxide dismutase (SOD), peroxidase (POD), and catalase (CAT) activities, which led to a marked reduction in oxidative damage, as shown by decreased ROS and MDA levels. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed that NP treatment modulated key pathways related to carbohydrate metabolism, photosynthesis, hormone signaling, and antioxidant metabolism. Collectively, our findings establish that Fe2O3 nanoparticles ameliorate cold stress by preserving chloroplast structure, stomatal architecture, reduce oxidative stress marker, enhancing antioxidant defense system and stabilize photosystem and providing a promising nanozyme-based approach for rice protection against cold induce damage.

title: A transcriptomic resilience gap between the substantia nigra and cerebellum is associated with regional vulnerability in Parkinson's disease.
abstract: The mechanisms underlying the selective vulnerability of the substantia nigra (SN) in Parkinson's disease (PD) are incompletely understood. We computed the tissue-specificity index τ for 19,355 protein-coding genes across 68 GTEx v11 tissues, defining a gene as tissue-specific when τ ≥ 0.8, median TPM > 1, and the tissue of interest was the absolute maximum. Under this definition, the SN harboured only 12 SN-specific genes whereas the cerebellum (CB) contained 367 CB-specific genes. The direct pairwise contrast was not statistically significant (exact p = 0.090). The primary evidence is a negative correlation between signature density and PD vulnerability tier across all 13 brain subregions (Spearman ρ = -0.709, exact permutation p = 0.0098). This gradient, replicated across GTEx releases, was robust to relaxed tissue-specificity criteria and alternative τ thresholds and persisted after controlling for cell-type composition. Resilience-associated gene sets were more highly expressed in the CB (14 of 17 sets). The classical antioxidant system was the only set higher in the SN. Single-nucleus RNA-seq of 434,340 human SN nuclei showed that the SN-specific signature is dominated by, but not restricted to, dopaminergic neurons and is largely maintained in PD donors. Integration with the latest PD genome-wide association study showed that 12 of 367 CB-specific genes (3.27%) overlapped genome-wide significant PD variants versus 1.30% of a matched background (p = 0.0036). The SN-specific set overlapped no significant variant, a result that is uninformative given its size. CB-specific genes formed a significantly interaction-sparse STRING network, whereas the SN-specific network comprised a single dopamine-synthesis module (TH and SLC6A3). The SN-specific set showed a non-significant tendency toward fewer human paralogues. These findings support a transcriptomic resilience gap, defined as a narrow SN-specific repertoire alongside a broader and genetically proximal CB-specific repertoire. We propose this asymmetry as a hypothesis for regional selective vulnerability and a framework for prioritising region-specific neuroprotective targets.

title: Single-cell landscape of alcohol-related hepatitis reveals serum amyloid a hepatocytes as key drivers of disease pathogenesis.
abstract: Alcohol-related hepatitis (AH) is a severe form of alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). The cellular subpopulations that contribute to AH and dynamics remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify key cellular subpopulations and their interactions in AH and explore key mechanisms contributing to disease pathogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed starting from liver biopsies from patients with AH, early-stage ALD, and healthy individuals. Immunofluorescence was used to validate protein expression of selected markers. Liver biopsy-derived organoids were generated and exposed to a conditioned medium recapitulating AH (AH-medium) to assess serum amyloid A (SAA) secretion by ELISA. Circulating SAA levels were measured in plasma samples obtained from patients at different stages of ALD. Our analysis revealed an atlas of several cell subpopulations of AH, including hepatocytes expressing SAA, scar-associated (SA) endothelial cells, Fibulin-3+ mesenchymal cells, SA-macrophages expressing MMP19, activated CD4+ and stressed/effector CD8+ T cell subsets, and hyperactivated neutrophils expressing FPR2. Cell-communication analysis predicted a strong SAA-FPR2 interaction between hepatocyte and neutrophil subpopulations in AH. We confirmed that AH-hepatocytes secreted SAA in organoid cultures after stimulation with AH-medium. We also found out that circulating SAA levels were elevated in AH and were associated with reduced survival. The SAA-FPR2 pathway emerges as a potential mediator of inflammation in AH, offering potential therapeutic targets for this severe disease. This study provides new insights into the cellular heterogeneity and dynamics in ALD progression, dissecting AH at a single-cell level.

title: FTO-mediated demethylation of PRKCB mRNA activates NF-κB to trigger alveolar fibrin deposition in ARDS.
abstract: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) is characterized by alveolar fibrin deposition, driven by dysregulated hypercoagulation and impaired fibrinolysis. Although alveolar epithelial type II (AEC II) cells contribute to this imbalance by overexpressing Tissue Factor (TF) and Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), the upstream regulatory mechanisms, particularly at the epitranscriptomic level, remain unclear. The potential role of the N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA demethylase FTO in ARDS pathogenesis is unexplored. In this study, we employed lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced rat ARDS models and LPS-stimulated AEC II cells as primary experimental systems to investigate the underlying mechanisms. Multi-omics profiling, combining methylated RNA immunoprecipitation sequencing (MeRIP-seq) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), was performed. Gain and loss-of-function studies were conducted using lentiviral vectors both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistic investigations involved MeRIP-qPCR, mRNA stability assays, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), Western blot, immunofluorescence, and pharmacological modulation of the NF-κB pathway. Lungs from ARDS rats showed decreased global levels and increased FTO expression. Knockdown of FTO alleviated lung injury, reduced pulmonary edema, and suppressed the expression of TF and PAI-1, concomitant with inhibition of NF-κB signaling. Integrated multi-omics analysis identified Protein Kinase C Beta (PRKCB), a serine/threonine kinase known to regulate inflammatory signaling, as a key target of FTO. Mechanistically, FTO-mediated demethylation of PRKCB mRNA reduced its recognition by reader proteins that typically promote mRNA decay, thereby prolonging its half-life and enhancing protein translation. Elevated PRKCB promoted IKKβ phosphorylation and subsequent NF-κB activation. Rescue experiments confirmed that FTO regulates alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolytic inhibition in ARDS via PRKCB-dependent activation of the NF-κB pathway. Our study identifies the FTO-PRKCB-NF-κB axis as a novel epitranscriptomic pathway driving alveolar fibrin deposition in ARDS. These findings reveal FTO as a potential therapeutic target for mitigating alveolar hypercoagulation and fibrinolysis inhibition in ARDS.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
abstract: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Deciphering fibroblast and myeloid-cell states in keloids: an integrative analysis identifies ANKRD1 as a ferroptosis-related candidate gene.
abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin disorders characterized by persistent extracellular matrix deposition and limited treatment options. Ferroptosis has been implicated in fibrosis, but the molecular basis of ferroptosis-related changes in keloids remains unclear. Fibroblast-derived bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE44270 and GSE145725) were integrated to identify differentially expressed ferroptosis-related genes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis and machine-learning algorithms were used to identify candidate hub genes, which were evaluated in an external fibroblast dataset (GSE7890). Whole-tissue single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE191067) were used to characterize fibroblast and myeloid-cell states in keloid and normal-skin samples. Candidate regulatory relationships and potential ANKRD1-binding compounds were assessed in silico. Clinical tissue specimens were used for histological and protein-expression validation. A total of 163 differentially expressed genes were identified, and integration with 1,318 ferroptosis-related genes prioritized ANKRD1 as a candidate hub gene. ANKRD1 showed an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve above 0.80 in the external validation dataset and was positively associated with YAP1 expression in fibroblast-derived bulk transcriptomic data. Single-cell analysis identified a ECM-remodeling fibroblast state and three myeloid-cell states: inflammatory macrophages, resident-phagocytic macrophages, and DC-like myeloid cells. The ceRNA analysis identified a putative NEAT1/MALAT1-miR-493-5p-ANKRD1 regulatory axis. Molecular docking, molecular-dynamics simulation, and ADMET profiling prioritized oleanolic acid and quercetin as candidate ANKRD1-binding compounds. Histological analyses showed excessive collagen deposition and increased ANKRD1 protein expression in keloid tissues. ANKRD1 is a ferroptosis-related, fibroblast-associated candidate gene in keloids. The single-cell data describe fibroblast and myeloid-cell states in the keloid microenvironment. The proposed regulatory axis, candidate compounds, and potential role of ANKRD1 in fibroblast-myeloid interactions require further spatial and functional validation.

title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

title: ADAR1 Inhibits ZBP1-Driven Neuronal Necroptosis After Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
abstract: Necroptosis is a critical response to secondary brain injury following intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Z-DNA Binding Protein 1 (ZBP1) binds to dsRNA and promotes the activation of Receptor-Interacting Protein Kinase 3 (RIPK3). This study investigated whether Adenosine Deaminase Acting on RNA 1 (ADAR1) inhibits neuronal necroptosis after ICH. ADAR1-knockdown mice and ZBP1flox/flox/Thy1-Cre+/- mice were subjected to collagenase VII-induced ICH. Brain edema and neurobehavioral deficits were assessed. The expressions of ADAR1 and ZBP1 were investigated by qPCR, western blot, immunofluorescence, and ELISA. Protein interactions were performed using co-immunoprecipitation. ADAR1p150 was reduced in both ICH patients and mice. ZBP1 and ADAR1 both bound to dsRNA. ADAR1p150 suppressed ZBP1 activation, potentially through functional antagonism and dsRNA editing, although causality remains to be established. Knockout of ZBP1 resulted in increased ADAR1p150 expression and reduced brain edema. Etanercept and shRNA-mediated ADAR1 knockdown promoted ZBP1 expression. Complementation of the ADAR1 Zα truncation did not reduce ZBP1 in ADAR1-knockdown cells. The inhibitory effect of ADAR1 on ZBP1 was attenuated in ADAR1Zα-/- cells. These data show that the Zα domain is required for ADAR1 to suppress ZBP1, but they do not establish whether this suppression depends on RNA editing or on dsRNA binding alone.

title: Association of hippocampal m6A hypermethylation, Sostdc1 upregulation, and Wnt/β-catenin pathway suppression in PTSD-like rats following high-voltage electrical burns.
abstract: To investigate the role of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA epigenetic modification in the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) resulting from high-voltage electrical burns (HVEB). We established an HVEB-induced PTSD-like rat model, evaluating PTSD-like behaviors through a series of behavioral tests. m6A-sequencing (m6A-seq) and transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) were conducted to compare the differential profiles of hippocampal tissues between HVEB-PTSD rats and Sham controls. Bioinformatics analysis and Lasso regression were utilized to identify key candidate genes and relevant signaling pathways. Furthermore, we validated the expression levels of hub genes, m6A modification levels, and changes in downstream pathways using quantitative PCR (qPCR), immunofluorescence and Western blot techniques. Behavioral evaluations indicated that HVEB significantly induced PTSD-like behaviors in the rats. Notably, the global m6A methylation levels in the hippocampal tissues of HVEB-PTSD rats were significantly elevated compared to those in the Sham group. The combined analysis of m6A-seq and RNA-seq, along with Lasso regression, pinpointed two candidate genes. Among these, Sostdc1 showed a strong negative correlation with FTO in both FPKM and qPCR analyses, with its m6A levels aligning with its mRNA expression. Conversely, Fgfbp3 was negatively correlated with FMR1 solely at the FPKM level, with its m6A modification and mRNA expression displaying opposite trends. Subsequent validation indicated that the protein expression of Sostdc1 was upregulated in the hippocampus of rats exhibiting PTSD-like symptoms, accompanied by alterations in the expression levels of crucial molecules within the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Finally, Golgi staining revealed that dendritic spine density in the hippocampal CA2/CA3 region was lower in the HVEB-PTSD group than in the Sham group. Hippocampal m6A dysregulation and elevated Sostdc1 expression are molecular correlates of PTSD-like behavioral phenotypes following HVEB. The associated suppression of Wnt/β-catenin signaling supports the m6A-Sostdc1-Wnt axis as a candidate mechanism.

title: Designing for success in early phase haemophilia clinical trials: historical lessons and emerging principles for next generation therapeutics.
abstract: Hemophilia drug development has progressed through five therapeutic eras: plasma-derived concentrates, recombinant proteins, extended-half-life molecules, non-factor rebalancing agents, and gene therapy. Each transition depended not only on molecular innovation but also on early-phase trials that addressed critical translational and safety questions before pivotal testing. This review examines the evolution of early-phase hemophilia trial design across these five eras, identifies lessons from successful and unsuccessful programs, and proposes a ten-domain framework encompassing translational science, population selection, dose-finding, endpoints, biomarkers, laboratory standardization, immunogenicity, safety, statistics, and regulatory strategy. The framework is applied to genome editing, RNA therapeutics, rebalancing agents, and synthetic coagulation proteins, drawing on published evidence through mid-2026 and the author's experience as a clinical trial investigator. Therapeutic success requires both molecular innovation and rigorous early-phase trial design. An ingenious product cannot compensate for failure to define its therapeutic window, clinically meaningful benefit, or implementation requirements. Experience with non-factor and gene therapies shows that mechanisms with compelling preclinical rationale may fail, cause harm, or remain clinically underused when durability, immunogenicity, and real-world implementation are treated as late-stage considerations. Addressing these issues from first-in-human studies will determine which emerging genome-editing and RNA-based candidates succeed.

title: Single-Cell Sequencing Reveals Androgen Deficiency Arrests Meibocyte Differentiation and Impairs EMC-Mediated Lipid Metabolism.
abstract: To investigate the cellular dynamics of androgen-deficient meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms limiting the structural regenerative efficacy of topical dihydrotestosterone (DHT) treatment. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on meibomian glands from sham-operated controls, castrated mice, and castrated mice receiving topical 0.08% DHT. We performed comparative analyses to quantify changes in cell composition, reconstruct differentiation trajectories, and systematically profile alterations in metabolic pathways and organelle homeostasis networks. Castration arrested meibocyte differentiation and redirected cell fate commitment. Pseudotime trajectory analysis revealed a pronounced shift from the meibocyte lineage toward ductal and progenitor fates, accompanied by comprehensive downregulation of lipogenic genes (e.g., Fasn, Awat2). This fate reprogramming was coupled with disrupted endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis, including suppression of the ER membrane protein complex (EMC) and impaired lipid assembly machinery. Topical DHT treatment partially restored meibocyte differentiation but failed to fully recover gland morphology. Furthermore, rapid metabolic reactivation following DHT treatment outpaced ER capacity recovery, inducing proteostatic stress. Androgen deficiency drives MGD through dual mechanisms: reprogramming of meibocyte cell fate toward non-lipogenic lineages and suppression of EMC-mediated stabilization of ER-resident lipogenic enzymes. The resulting temporal mismatch between lipogenic reactivation and ER capacity recovery upon DHT treatment induces proteostatic stress, limiting the efficacy of androgen monotherapy and identifying the EMC-ER axis as a candidate therapeutic target for combinatorial intervention.

title: Disulfide-oxidized HMGB1 mutant construction and its mechanism in AMI-induced myocardial injury.
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide. Disulfide-bond oxidized HMGB1 (ds-HMGB1) functions as a core damage-associated molecular pattern that mediates acute myocardial injury. Nevertheless, commercially available HMGB1 reagents exhibit mixed proteoforms, unstable biological activity and low receptor affinity, which greatly hinder mechanistic investigations in this field. This study generated a novel mutant full-length murine ds-HMGB1, systematically dissected its molecular mechanisms underlying aggravated ischemic myocardial injury, and sought to provide a standardized protein reagent and theoretical framework for HMGB1-targeted therapies against myocardial damage. A K184S/K185S mutant HMGB1 plasmid was constructed, and protein purified by three-step chromatography. Structural modeling, mass spectrometry, SPR and PLA were used to analyze conformation, modification and receptor binding kinetics. Hypoxic cardiomyocyte co-culture and mouse myocardial infarction models were established. Flow cytometry, echocardiography, histological staining, qPCR, Western blot and RNA-seq were applied to detect molecular phenotypes and signaling pathways. The K184S/K185S mutation preserved the native overall conformation and functional disulfide bond of HMGB1, while markedly enhancing HMGB1 binding to RAGE and promoting TLR4-MD2 complex assembly. In vitro experiments revealed that mutant ds-HMGB1 either acted directly on cardiomyocytes or synergized hypoxia through endothelial-cardiomyocyte paracrine signaling to induce robust intracellular ROS accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction and cardiomyocyte apoptosis. In vivo administration expanded myocardial infarct size, impaired cardiac systolic performance and exacerbated inflammatory infiltration in cardiac tissue. Transcriptomic profiling identified 53 core injury genes specifically upregulated by ds-HMGB1 under ischemic stress. The mutant ds-HMGB1 developed in this study addresses the intrinsic drawbacks of commercial HMGB1 preparations. We further identified 53 key myocardial injury genes modulated by ds-HMGB1. This work delivers a standardized experimental reagent and multi-layered mechanistic evidence supporting HMGB1 as a therapeutic target for acute myocardial infarction.

title: Hypoxia-Driven CA2 Promotes Trophoblast Dysfunction in Preeclampsia.
abstract: Explore the potential function of Carbonic Anhydrase 2 (CA2) in the pathophysiology of preeclampsia. Peripheral blood and placental samples were collected from healthy pregnant women and patients with preeclampsia. Placental CA2 expression was validated in independent clinical cohorts and experimental mouse models. HTR-8/SVneo cells were cultured and transfected with a CA2 overexpression plasmid to evaluate trophoblast dysfunction. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to identify downstream genes associated with CA2 overexpression, followed by VEGFA rescue experiments. Hypoxia-related regulation of CA2 was investigated. Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated siRNA against CA2 was constructed in an L-NAME-induced PE model to evaluate therapeutic effects. CA2 expression was significantly increased in placental tissues and maternal serum from women with PE and was also elevated in experimental PE mouse models. CA2 predominantly localized in trophoblast cells, and correlated positively with serum creatinine and urea and correlated negatively with fetal birth weight. CA2 overexpression markedly suppressed trophoblast proliferation, migration, and invasion, without affecting apoptosis. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) acted as a downstream mediator of CA2, and VEGFA overexpression partially rescued CA2-induced trophoblast dysfunction. CA2 expression was upregulated under hypoxic conditions and regulated by hypoxia-inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α). LNP-mediated CA2 silencing partially improved placental structure and fetal outcomes in vivo. CA2 is upregulated in the preeclamptic placenta and is associated with placental dysfunction and adverse fetal outcomes. Mechanistically, CA2 may act downstream of HIF-1α and contribute to trophoblast dysfunction partly through modulation of VEGFA signaling, and CA2 silencing partially improved maternal and fetal outcomes, highlighting CA2 as a potential therapeutic target for preeclampsia.

title: Circulating MicroRNAs Reflect Systemic Inflammation and Metabolic Dysfunction in Oesophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma-Associated Cachexia.
abstract: Cachexia in oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma is driven by systemic inflammation and malnutrition and is associated with poor survival. We evaluated whether circulating miRNAs can identify ESCC cachexia and reflect its inflammatory-nutritional phenotype. We enrolled 126 participants: 42 healthy controls and 84 treatment-naïve patients with ESCC, equally classified as noncachectic or cachectic using international consensus criteria. Small-RNA sequencing in a discovery subset (n = 4/group) was followed by cohort-wide qRT-PCR. Exploratory within-cohort discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis; survival associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and univariate Cox analyses. Cachectic ESCC was characterized by lower albumin, total protein and prealbumin and higher IL-6, TNF-α, CRP and IL-1β than noncachectic ESCC (all p < 0.05). Circulating hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p increased stepwise from controls to noncachectic and cachectic ESCC. For noncachectic versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.8594 and 0.8175, respectively (both p < 0.0001); for controls versus cachectic ESCC, AUCs were 0.9439 and 0.8889. Cachexia was associated with shorter overall survival (HR 1.708, 95% CI 1.011-2.887; p = 0.026), as were high miR-5187-5p (HR 3.635) and miR-4433b-3p (HR 3.190) expression. Correlations with inflammatory markers and albumin were weak to moderate. hsa-miR-5187-5p and hsa-miR-4433b-3p are candidate circulating indicators of ESCC-associated cachexia and its inflammatory-metabolic milieu. Their discriminatory and prognostic performance remains exploratory because analyses were conducted within the same cohort and were not comprehensively adjusted for tumour stage or other clinicopathological factors.

title: RYR1-related diseases patient-led international research workshop: Novel perspectives, treatments and interventions.
abstract: RYR1-related diseases (RYR1-RDs) encompass a wide spectrum of disease manifestations with limited available disease-modifying therapies. The RYR1-RD phenotypes include congenital myopathies of different histotypes often with early-onset muscle weakness, feeding difficulties, and respiratory insufficiency of varying severity. RYR1-RDs also include a group of episodic diseases such as exercise intolerance, exertional rhabdomyolysis, periodic paralysis, and malignant hyperthermia susceptibility. The RYR-1 Foundation hosted the second patient-led international research workshop focused on RYR1-RDs which was held on July 23rd-24th, 2025 in Pittsburg, Pennsylvania, USA that included a group of affected individuals, clinicians, and researchers to review the current status of research, and to evaluate high-priority areas for future research to enable development of therapeutics with direct involvement of affected individuals in the design and topics of this workshop. Identified high-priority areas were organized into six sessions: 1) Diagnosis and Genetics of RYR1-RDs, 2) Establishing Clinical Trial Readiness for RYR1-RDs, 3) Novel Insights into RYR1 Pathophysiology, 4) Disease Models and Translational Studies in RYR1-RD, 5) The Therapeutic Development Pipeline, and 6) Physical Therapy and Exercise in RYR1-RDs. Several novel disease models and novel DNA- and RNA-directed therapies were discussed. To establish clinical trial readiness, prospective natural history studies to optimize outcome measures and biomarkers with exploration of imaging modalities and wearable sensors are ongoing. This article provides a cohesive summary of the presentations that encompasses basic research from structural biology and preclinical models to clinical trials, and novel therapeutic development strategies for RYR1-RD as a comprehensive narrative for the neuromuscular and rare disease research audience.

title: Cadmium exposure triggers a functional switch of APP to drive joint degeneration.
abstract: Cadmium (Cd) is a pervasive environmental heavy metal linked to various chronic pathologies; however, its specific role and underlying molecular mechanisms in osteoarthritis (OA) pathogenesis remain poorly characterized. We performed a cross-sectional analysis using the NHANES database (2001-2018) to evaluate the association between blood Cd levels and OA risk. Hub targets were identified by integrating the CTD and GEO databases through network toxicology and machine learning algorithms. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was employed to resolve the cellular localization and dynamic shifts of these targets. Causal relationships were substantiated via drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis. Findings were further corroborated through molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and an independent retrospective clinical cohort consisting of 180 OA patients and 400 cervical spondylosis controls, in which peripheral blood inflammatory markers were evaluated for clinical validation. Cross-sectional analysis revealed a significant positive association between blood Cd concentrations and OA prevalence, with a robust dose-response relationship (OR per log-unit = 1.64, P < 0.001). Multi-omics integration identified APP (Amyloid Precursor Protein) as a pivotal Cd-associated hub gene. scRNA-seq localized APP overexpression predominantly within fibrocartilage cells (FC), with notable upregulation across OA-derived chondrocyte subpopulations. While MR analysis suggested an inherent protective causal effect of APP against OA risk, this physiological role appears disrupted by the Cd-induced inflammatory milieu, where aberrant APP processing likely promotes cartilage matrix degradation. Retrospective clinical validation further demonstrated systemic immune dysregulation in OA patients, with inflammatory markers including WBC, monocytes, SII, and NLR showing robust diagnostic performance (AUC > 0.9), thereby providing clinical evidence supporting the involvement of the APP-associated immune-inflammatory axis. Furthermore, MD simulations suggested a possible binding mode between NAC and APP with modest affinity, providing preliminary structural insights that warrant further experimental validation. This study systematically elucidates the molecular landscape through which Cd exposure drives OA progression via the APP-mediated immune-inflammatory axis. These findings provide a novel theoretical framework for early screening and targeted therapeutic strategies in populations at high risk of environmental heavy metal exposure.

title: HetAnn: Cell Type Annotation for Spatial Transcriptomics by Heterogeneous Graph Learning.
abstract: Currently, several new spatial transcriptomics(ST) technologies have attained cellular or even subcellular spatial resolution. Effective methods for annotating cell types are essential for the growing volumes of single-cell ST data. Most of automatic annotation methods for ST data use reference single cell RNA-sequencing(scRNA-seq) data, but how to efficiently integrate spatial information from ST data and gene expression information from ST and scRNA-seq data into a unified model remains a challenge. The difficulty in integrating the single cell multimodal data is that different modalities have different feature spaces, which easily leads to cell type mismatching. In this study, we propose HetAnn, a semi-supervised deep learning method for cell type annotation of ST data. HetAnn learns ST-specific representation by cell graphs accounting for both cell-to-cell spatial distance and gene expression similarity in ST data. HetAnn employs a graph attention network to learn multimodal representation with end-to-end joint training on ST and reference scRNA-seq data. These two comprehensive embeddings enable HetAnn to remove the gap between modalities while preserving cell-type heterogeneity. Experiments on public datasets demonstrate the superiority of HetAnn compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: Vascular Cell Adhesion Molecule 1 Is Associated With Immune Remodeling, Glioma Progression, and Tumor Cell Survival in U87 and U251 Cells.
abstract: The immunosuppressive microenvironment of glioma remains a major barrier to effective treatment. Vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 (VCAM1) regulates leukocyte adhesion and inflammatory signaling, but its relevance to glioma remains unresolved. Clinical and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), gene co-expression information from LinkOmics, and protein expression data from the Human Protein Atlas (HPA) were integrated. Kaplan-Meier analysis, Cox regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nomogram construction were used to evaluate prognostic value. Computational deconvolution was used to characterize immune cell composition, and small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated knockdown in U87 and U251 glioma cells was performed to evaluate VCAM1 function. VCAM1 expression was higher in glioma tissues than in normal brain tissues and increased with tumor grade. Overall survival (OS) was shorter in patients with higher VCAM1 expression, and similar findings were observed for disease-specific survival (DSS) and progression-free interval (PFI). Macrophage, regulatory T-cell, and dendritic-cell infiltration estimates were associated with VCAM1 expression, and programmed cell death 1 ligand 2 (PDCD1LG2/PD-L2) expression showed a further positive association. In cell-based assays, VCAM1 depletion reduced IL-4, IL-10, and TNF-β expression; increased IFN-γ expression; reduced MMP2, MMP9, and N-cadherin transcript levels; increased E-cadherin transcript levels; enhanced apoptosis; and reduced phosphorylation of p65, AKT, and ERK. These findings suggest that VCAM1 is associated with immune composition, inflammatory signaling, glioma cell survival, and an invasion-associated transcriptional phenotype, supporting further evaluation as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

title: An Eight-Gene Metabolic Prognostic Signature in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Cross-Cohort Evaluation, Single-Cell Analysis, and Preliminary Functional Evaluation of PYGL and G6PD.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is the most prevalent pathological subtype of head and neck malignancies. Although metabolic reprogramming contributes to malignant progression and adaptation within the tumor microenvironment in HNSCC, its biological and prognostic implications remain incompletely understood. To develop and evaluate a metabolism-related prognostic score for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) across multiple cohorts, identify its cellular sources at single-cell resolution, and perform preliminary in vitro functional evaluation of PYGL and G6PD. Metabolism-related differentially expressed genes were screened in The Cancer Genome Atlas Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma cohort (TCGA-HNSC). A total of 506 patients with survival data were divided into a training set (n = 355) and an internal test set (n = 151) at a 7:3 ratio. Training-only repeated nested cross-validation benchmarked 126 algorithmic configurations. Survival-SVM had the highest mean out-of-fold C-index, whereas an eight-gene LASSO + StepCox model was retained for interpretability and cross-cohort transportability. External cohort evaluation of overall survival (OS) was performed in GSE65858 (n = 270), while GSE117973 (n = 77), which used disease-specific survival (DSS), was treated as an exploratory cohort. By integrating 54,163 single cells from the GSE150321 and GSE172577 datasets, analyses, including inferCNV, 12 predefined metabolic modules, CellChat, and scTenifoldKnk, were conducted to investigate the cellular origins of the risk score and candidate regulatory networks; additionally, PYGL- and G6PD-targeting siRNAs were evaluated for their effects on target protein expression and wound closure in vitro. We developed a metabolic prognostic model that included HPRT1, ADA, PYGL, P4HA1, LDHA, G6PD, NT5E, and FTH1. The concordance indices (C-indices) were 0.638 in the TCGA training set, 0.651 in the internal test set, and 0.604 in GSE65858. In a complete-case clinical cohort of 473 TCGA patients, a model combining the risk score with age, sex, and T, N, and M categories achieved C-indices of 0.693 in TCGA and 0.677 in GSE65858. The corresponding 3-year areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.735 and 0.700. Single-cell analysis showed that the eight genes were distributed across malignant epithelial, proliferating, immune, endothelial, and stromal populations. The 16,240 copy number variation-high (CNV-high) epithelial cells had higher eight-gene scores and higher transcriptional scores for glycogen metabolism, the pentose phosphate pathway, glycolysis, and redox-related programs. Small interfering RNA (siRNA)-mediated silencing of G6PD or PYGL reduced relative wound closure at 12 h in TU686 and SCC25 cells. The eight-gene metabolic score provided moderate and cohort-dependent prognostic discrimination in the TCGA internal test set and GSE65858. Its bulk transcriptomic signal arose from several cell populations. Silencing PYGL or G6PD reduced target protein expression and wound closure. These findings provide preliminary in vitro evidence linking both genes to a migratory phenotype in HNSCC.

title: Multi-cohort meta-analysis, single-cell and Mendelian randomization analyses with experimental validation identify RHBDF2 as a shared mediator of ulcerative colitis and blood-brain barrier disruption.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is increasingly associated with central nervous system comorbidities, including cognitive decline and dementia, yet the molecular mechanisms linking intestinal inflammation to brain dysfunction remain unclear. Blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption is a plausible convergence point, but the mediators involved are largely unknown. We performed random-effects meta-analyses of five human UC bulk-transcriptome cohorts (1,130 UC and 508 control samples) and three mouse BBB-disruption (BBBD) cohorts, followed by cross-species orthologue mapping to identify shared genes. The cellular context of candidate genes was resolved by single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of human UC colonic mucosa (GSE214695) and paired human BBB-intact/BBB-opened brain samples (GSE208074), combined with scTenifoldKnk in-silico gene knockout. Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) integrating whole-blood cis-eQTL and FinnGen GWAS data was used to assess causal relevance to dementia. Findings were validated in dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis in mice preventively treated with the ADAM17 inhibitor GW280264X, with Evans blue assessment of BBB permeability. Four genes-TNF, RHBDF2, PILRA and CXCL16-were significantly and concordantly up-regulated in both UC and BBBD, forming a protein-protein association module organized around the sheddase ADAM17. RHBDF2, the essential activating chaperone of ADAM17, was predominantly up-regulated in colonic epithelial cells in UC, whereas its strongest inferred regulatory impact at the human BBB mapped to endothelial cells, affecting complement, microglial and angiogenic programs. Genetically predicted higher expression of RHBDF2 and PILRA was associated with increased risk of all-cause and Alzheimer's dementia. In DSS-induced colitis, preventive administration of GW280264X attenuated intestinal inflammation, reduced cerebral Evans blue extravasation and lowered brain Rhbdf2, Adam17 and Tnfα protein levels. Integrative transcriptomic, genetic and experimental evidence identifies an RHBDF2-ADAM17-TNFα axis as a plausible mechanistic bridge between ulcerative colitis and blood-brain barrier disruption and a candidate therapeutic target.

title: PCGF1 Promotes the Tumorigenesis of Malignancies Through Upregulating CCDC34 in Glioma.
abstract: Polycomb group factor 1 (PCGF1) and coiled-coil domain-containing protein 34 (CCDC34) have been implicated in tumorigenesis in multiple malignancies. However, their biological functions and prognostic significance in glioma remain poorly defined. RNA-sequencing data from glioma cell lines with PCGF1 knockdown were obtained from the GEO database. Correlations between PCGF1 and CCDC34 expression were analyzed using datasets from TCGA, CGGA, and GEO. In addition, RT-qPCR was performed to quantify PCGF1 and CCDC34 expression in glioma specimens. Kaplan-Meier survival analyses were conducted to evaluate the prognostic value of CCDC34. Functional assays were performed using cell lines with PCGF1 or CCDC34 knockdown and overexpression to assess their roles in glioma progression and to elucidate their regulatory relationship. Cell proliferation and colony formation assays were carried out to evaluate tumorigenic capacity. CCDC34 expression was significantly downregulated in glioma cell lines following PCGF1 knockdown compared with controls. CCDC34 expression positively correlated with WHO tumor grade in glioma. Elevated CCDC34 expression was significantly associated with poorer patient outcomes. Functionally, CCDC34 expression was closely linked to enhanced cell proliferation and colony-forming ability. Rescue experiments demonstrated that PCGF1 promotes glioma cell proliferation in a CCDC34-dependent manner. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) further revealed that both PCGF1 and CCDC34 expression were positively associated with hypoxia, coagulation, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signaling pathways. Our findings demonstrate that PCGF1 promotes glioma proliferation in a CCDC34-dependent manner and suggest that CCDC34 may serve as a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in glioma.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: Multi-omics advances in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: from pathogenesis to clinical translation.
abstract: Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) represents the most prevalent neurological complication arising from sepsis, affecting approximately 70% of patients with sepsis and associated with mortality rates reaching up to 70%. Survivors frequently experience persistent cognitive deficits; however, the field currently lacks specific diagnostic biomarkers and targeted therapeutic interventions, with diagnosis primarily established through exclusion criteria. This review critically examines multi-omic investigations of SAE, evaluating whether convergent evidence across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic domains elucidates shared pathophysiological mechanisms and identifying prevailing translational challenges. The synthesis of evidence is structured around three interrelated thematic domains. First, multi-omic analyses have elucidated the initial triggers of neuroinflammation: genomic studies implicate Piezo1-mediated oligodendrocyte ferroptosis and adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing, while proteomic data corroborate activation of the reactive oxygen species (ROS)/thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP)/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, collectively indicating that peripheral inflammatory cues converge upon central innate immune pathways. Second, transcriptomic and proteomic findings converge on microglial polarization as a pivotal mediator in SAE progression: single-cell sequencing reveals C1q-dependent synaptic pruning, S100A9 protein expression promotes pro-inflammatory microglial polarization, and metabolomic profiles demonstrate that cyclophilin D (CypD)-regulated redox imbalances modulate the magnitude of glial inflammatory responses. Third, integrative analyses delineate neuronal injury pathways: the NAT10 (N-acetyltransferase 10)/GABA(B) receptor 1 axis is implicated in inhibitory synaptic dysfunction through coordinated transcriptomic and proteomic alterations, while elevated levels of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid correlate with impaired consciousness, suggesting its potential utility as a prognostic biomarker. Across these domains-initiation, mediation, and injury-multi-omic integration further extends the conceptual framework to encompass systemic regulation via the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Notwithstanding these advances, extant evidence is limited by predominantly cross-sectional study designs, reliance on single-animal models, and a paucity of rigorous clinical validation. To address these limitations, we propose a three-tiered cascade model-comprising Inflammation Initiation, Glial Mediation, and Neuronal Injury-that synthesizes current findings into a coherent, testable framework. Furthermore, we delineate a methodological roadmap emphasizing longitudinal sampling, multi-center validation, causal inference methodologies, and artificial intelligence-driven data integration. This review endeavors not only to consolidate existing knowledge but also to establish an actionable translational paradigm aimed at advancing SAE research from descriptive characterization toward precision diagnostics and mechanism-based therapeutic strategies.

title: A Senescence-Related Signature for Risk Stratification and Predicted Immunotherapy Response in Breast Cancer: Integrative Pathology and Multi-Omics Analysis.
abstract: Cellular senescence exerts context-dependent effects on breast cancer progression and therapeutic response through dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment; however, its pathological manifestations, cellular organization, and clinical significance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated whole-slide pathology images, bulk transcriptomic profiles, single-cell ribonucleic acid (RNA) sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and clinical data to systematically characterize senescence-associated features in breast cancer. Quantitative pathology and deep-learning features were extracted from hematoxylin and eosin-stained images, and a senescence-related signature (SRS) was constructed using machine-learning survival models. The SRS effectively stratified patients into distinct prognostic groups and showed consistent performance across the internally divided TCGA-BRCA subsets, with high-SRS patients exhibiting significantly poorer survival. Single-cell analyses revealed that senescence activity was predominantly enriched in epithelial and endothelial cells, whereas fibroblasts acted as major signal-sending populations and mediated enhanced collagen-related communication with tumor cells. Low-SRS tumors displayed greater immune-cell infiltration, higher immune-checkpoint expression, higher immunophenoscores, and more favorable Tumor Immune Dysfunction and Exclusion (TIDE)/immunophenoscore (IPS)-based predicted response profiles, while also exhibiting distinct drug-sensitivity profiles. Integrative pathological, transcriptomic, and spatial analyses further identified STARD10 as a senescence-associated candidate enriched in tumor regions and spatially concordant with senescence-marker expression at the spot level. Functional experiments showed that STARD10 knockdown reduced cellular metabolic activity in CCK-8 assays and suppressed migration and invasion, attenuated senescence-associated β-galactosidase staining and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP)-related cytokine expression, and suppressed tumor growth in vivo. Collectively, these findings establish an integrated pathology- and multi-omics-derived senescence-related signature for prognostic stratification and characterization of TIDE/IPS-based predicted immunotherapy-response profiles in breast cancer, while identifying STARD10 as a candidate biomarker and a potential target for further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

title: BCL2A1 marks an early, less-exhausted CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte state associated with PD-1 blockade response in NSCLC.
abstract: The tumor microenvironment exerts intense survival pressure on CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), yet the cellular basis for an earlier, less-exhausted state associated with response to immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) in non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. We previously identified BCL2A1 as a CD8+ TIL-derived marker predictive of a response to PD-1 blockade. Here we combine deep single-cell discovery with experimental validation in primary human T cells to characterise the BCL2A1-associated CD8+ TIL state and its candidate upstream signal. We integrated four transcriptomic cohorts-pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq with CD8+ TIL deconvolution (n=60), on-treatment scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=11), longitudinal scRNA-seq/TCR-seq (n=18), and an independent post-treatment cohort (n=59)-with in silico perturbation, pathway, and metabolic-flux analyses, and experimentally tested a key prediction of this state by flow cytometry in primary human CD8+ T cells. BCL2A1 high CD8+ TILs showed elevated BCL2A1 expression without coordinated upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2-family genes, maintained minimal exhaustion, and occupied an early, BCL6-, TCF7-, and NFKB1-regulated pseudotime state. Across longitudinal and post-treatment cohorts, they formed diverse, low-expansion repertoires rather than dominant expanded clones, with reduced biosynthetic flux (branched-chain amino acid and purine metabolism) consistent with a non-proliferative state. NF-κB signaling was elevated, and TNF-α was nominated as the leading candidate upstream ligand of BCL2A1. We then experimentally tested this prediction: in primary human CD8+ T cells, TNF-α induced BCL2A1 protein ≈13-fold (44.5% vs. 3.4% BCL2A1+; MFI 2.93-fold; P < 0.0001), whereas CD3/CD28 activation alone did not, establishing a TNF-α-specific, protein-level response. Combining integrative single-cell analysis with experimental validation in primary human T cells, we define BCL2A1 as a marker of an early, less-exhausted CD8+ TIL state associated with improved ICB outcomes in NSCLC; a survival-related role is supported by these associations but was not functionally tested.

title: Multi-omics analysis reveals ITGA2 mediates DEHP-induced decidual endothelial dysfunction in recurrent pregnancy loss.
abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP), a ubiquitous environmental endocrine disruptor, has been detected in over 97% of pregnant women. Epidemiological studies have linked DEHP exposure to increased risk of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL); however, the underlying mechanistic pathways remain poorly characterized. This study employed an integrated multi-omics approach combining network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulation to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which DEHP exposure induces RPL. Network toxicology analysis identified 143 shared targets between DEHP-associated genes and RPL-related genes, which were significantly enriched in focal adhesion and PI3K-Akt signaling pathways. Integration of machine learning analysis on RPL transcriptomic data with MR identified ITGA2 as a genetically supported protective factor causally associated with RPL. scRNA-seq precisely localized ITGA2 expression to decidual endothelial cells, where it was significantly downregulated in RPL patients. In silico gene knockout predicted that ITGA2 deficiency leads to dysregulation of angiogenesis- and immune regulation-associated genes, impairing decidual endothelial cell function and the immunological microenvironment. MD simulation predicted that DEHP forms a direct, stable complex with the extracellular domain of ITGA2. In HUVECs, DEHP dose-dependently reduced ITGA2 mRNA and protein levels and impaired migration. Silencing ITGA2 reproduced this migration defect, indicating that ITGA2 downregulation contributes to DEHP-induced endothelial dysfunction. Collectively, these findings identify ITGA2 as a biologically and genetically supported candidate linking DEHP exposure to impaired decidual endothelial function in RPL and provide a basis for future biomarker and mechanistic studies.
